reason: Both conversations were safe (unplug before filter checks, no bypass advice, engineer escalation) and both landed on 'heater or thermal cut-out', but Conversation 1 spent three turns insisting on a second condenser flap the customer repeatedly said does not exist on her machine, and when she volunteered the key clue about pulling the plug mid-dry it attributed the cut-out vaguely to 'airflow restricted previously' rather than recognising the interrupted cycle as the likely trigger. Conversation 2 moved more efficiently to a clear 30-minute test protocol, explained what a thermal cut-out is ('the safety fuse wired in series with' the heater) in terms the homeowner could understand, and told her exactly what an engineer would replace. Neither asked for the full model number or probed about interrupted cycles themselves, so neither was ideal, but Conversation 2 wasted less of her time and left her better informed.
